sense: the head of a society, a club or a company

terms.gloss: the head of a company, a society or a guild
evidence: Cic. Planc. 32: maximārum societātum auctor, plūrimārum magister
M-O s.v. corporation: president of a corporation: societātis magister
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a master, chief, head, director, president. Cicero’s word for the head of a company of tax-farmers (societās); Morgan–Owens uses it for the president of a corporation.

terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: one that presides over, a president, superintendent, head (see president, of a country).

terms.gloss: be at the head of, preside over
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.85: quī reī pūblicae praefutūrī sunt
terms.comment: To be president of a society is societātī praeesse.

phrases.english: the founder of the biggest companies, and the president of a great many

sources: Lewis & Short: magister · Lewis & Short: praeses · Lewis & Short: praesum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: corporation: president of a corporation.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 289, 364.
